results.nl: An assessment whose purpose value is Diagnostic is inferred to be a Diagnostic Assessment (purpose-axis sufficient condition; the prompt-v2 worked example is this very bridge pattern).
An assessment whose scores are interpreted against fixed criteria is inferred to be a Criterion-Referenced Test (score-interpretation-axis sufficient condition).

An assessment whose purpose value is Diagnostic is inferred to be a Formative Assessment, two steps: DiagnosticPurpose is subsumed by FormativePurpose (corpus-dominant reading), so the purpose-bridge realizes the individual into the formative defined class.

A self-assessment is inferred to be a Formative Assessment (SelfAssessment < DiagnosticAssessment < FormativeAssessment; each step is a verbatim corpus sentence). Deliberate A<C ceiling probe: SelfAssessment is low-production (4/20) but corpus-quoted, so the C configuration can evidence-gate it in.

An individual that has a learning outcome and a norm-referenced score interpretation is inferred to be a Norm-Referenced Test via domain(hasLearningOutcome)=Assessment then Assessment + norm-referenced = Norm-Referenced Test (two-step realization without an asserted Assessment type).

A formal assessment necessarily has some assessment item: an individual asserted to be a Formal Assessment inherits the existential obligation hasItem some AssessmentItem (corpus: 'Formal assessment usually implies a written document, such as a test, quiz, or paper').
Concurrent Validity is a form of Validity (ConcurrentValidity < CriterionValidity < Validity; two-level asserted chain over the corpus-natural root).

A Diagnostic Assessment is a Formative Assessment (inferred through the purpose axis: DiagnosticPurpose < FormativePurpose plus the two equivalentClass bridges; the corpus-dominant reading 'A common form of formative assessment is diagnostic assessment').
Test-Retest Reliability is a form of Reliability (direct corpus-natural subsumption; replaces the dead MeasurementProperty superclass probe).
A Multiple-Choice Item is an Assessment Item (MultipleChoiceItem < SelectedResponseItem < AssessmentItem).
An Essay Item is an Assessment Item (EssayItem < ConstructedResponseItem < AssessmentItem).
A reliability estimate cannot be both Test-Retest Reliability and Inter-Rater Reliability (reliability subtypes are pairwise disjoint).
A rubric cannot be both an Analytic Rubric and a Holistic Rubric (rubric kinds are disjoint).
An item cannot be both a Multiple-Choice Item and an Essay Item (selected-response and constructed-response families are disjoint).
A test cannot be both a High-Stakes Test and a Low-Stakes Test (the corpus contrasts the pair as exclusive alternatives; both names are 17/20 system-natural).

An assessment cannot be both a Formative Assessment and a Summative Assessment (disjointness INFERRED from the functional purpose axis plus the disjoint union of purpose values — the coherence-critical partition probed directly on bridge names).
An assessment cannot have two distinct purpose values (hasPurpose is functional / exactly one).
An assessment cannot have two distinct score-interpretation values (hasScoreInterpretation is functional).
A reliability estimate cannot report two different coefficient values (hasReliabilityCoefficient is a functional datatype property: one estimate, one coefficient).

Declaring an individual Diagnostic Assessment is consistent (trap-1 sensitivity probe: encoding the corpus's coordinate 4-way disjoint list TOGETHER WITH 'diagnostic is a common form of formative assessment' makes DiagnosticAssessment unsatisfiable; the gold resolves the tension by subordination, so the individual must be admissible).

Declaring an individual Interim Assessment is consistent (trap-2 sensitivity probe: encoding both sides of the corpus's open debate — interim as formative AND as summative — under the formative/summative partition makes InterimAssessment unsatisfiable; the gold keeps it neutral and satisfiable).

Being a Standardized Test AND a Formative Assessment simultaneously is consistent (trap-3 sensitivity probe; corpus: 'Formative assessments can take the form of diagnostic, standardized tests, quizzes, oral questions, or draft work' — a standardized-formative individual must be admissible, so any formative<informal / standardized<formal over-encoding is penalized).

Declaring an individual Multiple-Response Item is consistent (trap-4 sensitivity probe: defining objective assessment by a single-correct-answer cardinality while listing multiple-response among objective types makes MultipleResponseItem unsatisfiable; the gold documents the tension without the cardinality definition).

Being standardized AND high-stakes simultaneously is a legitimate (consistent) combination — the corpus states it verbatim: 'a test can be both standardized and also a high-stakes test' (also penalizes over-generalizing 'Most standardized tests ... are low-stakes tests' into an axiom).
